# Build handover, 2026-11-03 (M5)

M5 of `docs/11-build-plan.md`, source control, testing and the first real ticket, is built on branch `m5`, with a
milestone pull request into `main` awaiting review. The live run met the done-when: a real ticket merged by the
engine into a non-default parent branch on the fixture. LOG 107 to 146 are unreviewed (section 3). This continues
`handover-2026-11-03.md`, written earlier the same day for M0 to M4.

## 1. State

| Milestone | Merged | Results note | Tests (default / integration / live) |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 to M4 | `9279026` and earlier | `m0-results.md` to `m4-results.md` | 392 / 31 / 6 at M4 |
| SP1 flake fix, LOG 91 to 106 approval | `4c5d092` (pull requests 3 and 4) | | |
| M5 | Not yet: branch `m5`, milestone pull request into `main` | `m5-results.md` | 741 / 50 / 21 plus the live run |

M5 was built as three pieces, each reviewed independently and fixed before it was merged into `m5`: the interfaces
and in-memory fakes; the providers (pull request 5); the engine actions and checks (pull request 6). The integration
added the engine-level SP4 test, the budget for `unauthenticated` and `forbidden`, and the live run.

**The live run** (`m5-results.md`, "Integration"): run `run-2bcdfbd1e2e5` took ticket M5-LIVE-1 (widget names at
most 100 characters) from start to an engine squash merge, `4444a11`, into `ff/epic/m5-live`, with a `haiku`
planner, implementer and five reviewers, and CI evidence for the merged head (unit tier 8 passed). `main` was not
touched. Its references were deleted afterwards. The same start without `--parent-branch` was refused at run start
(F1, check 23). A first attempt stopped because std's review task did not say that only `Read` counts as opening a
file; the task was fixed (LOG 145) and the run repeated.

## 2. How M5 was run

As section 2 of the earlier handover: a builder per piece in its own worktree and branch, an independent reviewer
given the code, fixes with tests and controls, and merges with a merge commit once CI is green. Pieces went into the
milestone branch `m5` through pull requests 5 and 6; the milestone goes into `main` through one more, pull request 7, whose independent review's fixes are in. Controls for
the engine side are in `tools/check_m5_actions_controls.py` (59, all hold).

## 3. Open for the product owner

**LOG 107 to 146.** One line each. **Look** marks the ones that need the product owner's eye; "Coordinator" notes a
decision already taken.

|---|---|---|

| 108 | The Git provider builds merges in a bare clone cache (git 2.38 or later); engine commits are authored "Feature Flow" | |
| 109 | One pooled HTTPS client for GitHub; one connection per `git` command | Coordinator: enough for version 1 |

| 111 | GitHub pull requests adopted by a hidden key marker; reverts are GitHub's own | |

| 113 | Which CI runs to expect is read from the workflow files' triggers at the revision | |
| 114 | The engine's GitHub token may write Actions (to dispatch); agents unchanged | |
| 115 | CI result files are found in a run's artifacts by name | |

## 4. Access and environment

As section 4 of `handover-2026-11-03.md`, with these additions.

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| A live `ticket_delivery` run | `m5-results.md`, "The live run (M5's done-when): how to". Run the three hosts with one installation and organisation; the CLI is `src/FeatureFlow.Cli` (`ff`), with `--api` and `--token-file` |
| The fixture's `main` | Protected by the ruleset `protect-main`: a pull request with 0 approvals, no force-push, no bypass. The engine never merges there unless the organisation lists the repository in `engine_may_merge` |
| Temporal ports used | 8833 for the M5 integration |
| The fixture after M5 | Only `main`, at `1610c66` (the coordinator deleted the merged `ff/manifest-v1`); closed pull requests stay as history |
